mainTopic: The end of the בכור לדבר אחד debate, and the new משנה about an animal bought from a גוי: when do we rely on רוב?
overview: The amud opens by finishing an argument about the בכור. רבינא holds that an animal that is first in only one way still counts as a בכור. He reads the extra word 'בכור' as excluding a baby born after a caesarean-born sibling. רב אחא מדפתי brings a case this cannot explain: a female born by caesarean, then a male through the womb. So the גמרא concludes like אביי: a בכור לדבר אחד is not a בכור, and the פרק הלוקח עובר פרתו ends. A new משנה deals with an animal bought from a גוי whose birth history is unknown. רבי ישמעאל decides by the animal's age, while רבי עקיבא says only real knowledge counts, and in a ספק the owner eats the animal once it has a מום. The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל doesn't simply follow the רוב of animals, and suggests a difference between a majority in front of us and one that is not. A ברייתא about minors doing יבום challenges that difference, and רבא begins a new answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבינא explains what the word 'firstborn' comes to exclude
steps.stepSummary: Per רבינא, the word 'בכור' cannot be needed to exclude a male born after a female, since 'פטר רחם' already teaches that. So it must exclude a male born after a יוצא דופן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the word 'firstborn' came to exclude a case where a female came out before this male, we already learn that from 'opens the womb.' So we learn that 'firstborn' excludes an animal born after a caesarean-born sibling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבינא's explanation. It shows that the word 'בכור' has a job left to do: excluding a baby born after a caesarean-born sibling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a female came out of the womb first, the male did not 'open the womb,' so 'פטר רחם' already excludes him. That leaves the word 'בכור' free for something else. רבינא says it excludes a baby born through the womb after an older sibling came out by caesarean.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude (a case from a law)
'that which opens the womb': the first to come out of the womb
it is derived (from a source)
learn from this; conclude from it
one born through the side (caesarean birth)

phrases.english: If it is to exclude a case
where a female came out before it
that is already derived from 'opens the womb'!
Rather, learn from this that 'firstborn'
comes to exclude a case where one comes out
after a caesarean-born one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְמַעוֹטֵי הֵיכָא דְּיָצְתָה נְקֵבָה לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבינא's reading of the ברייתא from the earlier part of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבינא, the extra word 'בכור' excludes an animal born through the womb after a sibling born by caesarean.

steps.title: רב אחא grants that רבינא's reading works for one case
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי agrees that רבינא's view explains a male born by caesarean followed by a male through the womb. That second male is 'firstborn of the womb' but not 'firstborn of the males.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: If you think a firstborn in one respect counts as a firstborn, that is fine where a male came out by caesarean and then a male came through the womb. That one is not holy because the word 'firstborn' excludes it. It is first from the womb, but it is not the first of the males.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא is setting up a challenge. First he shows the one case where רבינא's reading works well, and in the next step he will show a case where it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the second male opened the womb, so he is first in one way. But a male was already born before him, so he is not the first male. The word 'בכור' can fairly exclude him, as רבינא said.

keyTerms.meaning: if it enters your mind; if you think
a firstborn in only one respect
it works out well (setup before 'but...')
first to come out of the womb
first of the male offspring

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
If it enters your mind
that a firstborn in one respect is a firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: תִּינַח הֵיכָא דְּיָצָא זָכָר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן
phrases.english: that works out well where a male came out by caesarean
and a male came through the womb, that it is not holy,
because this birth is excluded by 'firstborn,'
since there is a firstborn of the womb,
but there is no firstborn of the males.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר, תִּינַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to רבינא's reading by first granting the case it explains.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's view that a בכור לדבר אחד is a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: shows the case that fits, before presenting the case that does not.

steps.title: The case רבינא's reading cannot explain
steps.stepSummary: If a female came out by caesarean and then a male through the womb, the male is first in both ways. רבינא's reading leaves nothing to exclude him, so he should be holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where a female came out through the side and a male came through the womb, it should be holy, since it is both the first of the males and the first of the womb!
steps.whatsHappening: Here רב אחא lands his challenge. He brings a case where רבינא's reading would make the male holy, which does not fit the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The male is the first male, and he is also the first to open the womb. 'פטר רחם' does not exclude him. The word 'בכור' does not exclude him either, because he is fully first of the males and first of the womb. So רבינא has no source for excluding him, even though the ברייתא does not treat him as a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: through the side (by caesarean)
through the womb (normal birth)
let it be sanctified (a challenge: 'it should be holy!')

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In step 2 the first animal born by caesarean was a male, and in this step it is a female. That difference is the whole challenge.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּיָצְתָה נְקֵבָה דֶּרֶךְ דּוֹפֶן
phrases.english: But where a female came out through the side
and a male came through the womb
let it be holy,
phrases.notes: This is said as a challenge: by רבינא's logic this male should be holy, but he isn't.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אִיכָּא בְּכוֹר לִזְכָרִים וּבְכוֹר לְרֶחֶם!
phrases.english: since it is both the first of the males and the first of the womb!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּיָצְתָה נְקֵבָה דֶּרֶךְ דּוֹפֶן וְזָכָר דֶּרֶךְ רֶחֶם לִיקְדַּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's reading that the word 'בכור' is extra and excludes only a baby born after a male יוצא דופן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the female-then-male case, the male is first in both ways. רבינא has no source to exclude him, yet the ברייתא does not treat him as a בכור.

steps.title: Conclusion: the ברייתא is explained like אביי
steps.stepSummary: Because רבינא's reading cannot explain every case, the גמרא concludes that the ברייתא must be read like אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the explanation is like אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבינא's approach and settles on אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, an animal that is first in only one way is not a בכור at all. That explains both cases: whenever any sibling, male or female, came out by caesarean first, the next animal is not first in every way, so it is not a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clear (the גמרא's final decision)
like אביי (according to his explanation)

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion follows אביי: a בכור לדבר אחד is not a בכור. An animal must be first in every way, with no earlier birth of any kind, male or female, caesarean or not, to have בכור holiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halacha that an animal must be a full firstborn in every way to be holy as a בכור.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear that it is like Abaye.
phrases.notes: This goes back to אביי's view from earlier on the דף: being first in only one way is not enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב אחא's challenge and rejects רבינא's approach.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A בכור לדבר אחד is not a בכור, as אביי said.

steps.title: הדרן: closing the chapter הלוקח עובר פרתו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק הלוקח עובר פרתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'One Who Buys the Fetus of His Cow.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line formally ends the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן shows love for the learning and the hope of coming back to review it. The next פרק starts fresh with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (formula for finishing a פרק)
'one who buys the fetus of his cow': the name of this פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One Who Buys the Fetus of His Cow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק הלוקח עובר פרתו.

steps.title: The new משנה: buying an animal from a non-Jew, and רבי ישמעאל's age rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes an animal bought from a גוי with an unknown birth history. רבי ישמעאל rules by age: below a set age, its next male offspring is surely a בכור for the כהן; above that age, it is a ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone buys an animal from a non-Jew and doesn't know whether it ever gave birth. רבי ישמעאל says: a goat in its first year, its offspring surely goes to the priest; after that it's uncertain. A sheep in its first two years, surely to the priest; after that, uncertain. A cow or donkey in its first three years, surely to the priest; after that, uncertain.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a case: we bought an animal and don't know if it already had a baby. רבי ישמעאל uses the animal's age to decide whether its next male is a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the first birth of a mother can produce a בכור. רבי ישמעאל assumes that animals below a certain age (one year for a goat, two for a sheep, three for a cow or donkey) have not given birth yet. Past that age they might have, so the status of the next male is a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: She already gave birth for the first time (so her next offspring is not a firstborn)
Definitely belongs to the כהן as a בכור
An uncertain case
A goat / a ewe (female sheep)

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who buys an animal from a non-Jew,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אִם בִּיכְּרָה אִם לֹא בִּיכְּרָה.
phrases.english: and does not know whether it has given birth before or has not given birth before.
Rabbi Yishmael says:
A goat in its first year: its offspring definitely goes to the priest;
from here on, it is uncertain.
A ewe in its first two years: definitely to the priest;
from here on, it is uncertain.

phrases.aramaic: פָּרָה וַחֲמוֹר בְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ — וַדַּאי לַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: A cow or a donkey in their first three years: definitely to the priest;
from here on, it is uncertain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new perek after the הדרן closing in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, below a set age per species the animal surely has not given birth, so its next male is a certain בכור; above that age it is a ספק.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: signs of a pregnancy also count, so age proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי ישמעאל. An animal loses its first-birth status through signs of a pregnancy even without a live baby, so even a young animal may already have lost it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If only a live baby exempted an animal, you would be right. But the Sages said: the sign of a baby in a small animal is a murky discharge, in a large animal an afterbirth, and in a woman a fetal sac or an afterbirth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back on רבי ישמעאל's age rule. Something smaller than a full birth can also end the animal's chance to have a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's age rule works only if a live birth is the only thing that counts. But a discharge or an afterbirth also shows the animal was pregnant, and that can happen even in the first year. So a young age does not prove the next male is a certain בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Is exempted (no longer able to produce a בכור)
Small animal (sheep, goat) / large animal (cow, donkey)
A murky discharge from the womb
Afterbirth
A fetal sac

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ בְּוָולָד בִּלְבַד הַבְּהֵמָה נִפְטֶרֶת כִּדְבָרֶיךָ,
phrases.english: If an animal were exempted only by giving birth to a baby, it would be as you say,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמְרוּ: סִימָן הַוָּולָד בִּבְהֵמָה דַּקָּה — טִינּוּף,
phrases.english: but they said: the sign of a baby in a small animal is a murky discharge,
and in a large animal, an afterbirth,
and in a woman, a fetal sac or an afterbirth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אִילּוּ בְּוָולָד בִּלְבַד הַבְּהֵמָה נִפְטֶרֶת כִּדְבָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל's age rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's assumption that a young animal surely has not lost its first-birth status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Signs of a pregnancy (discharge, afterbirth) also exempt the animal, and these can occur early, so a young age does not prove anything.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's general rule: known, not known, and uncertain
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's rule: if the animal is known to have given birth, the כהן gets nothing. If it is known that it did not, the offspring goes to the כהן. If it is a ספק, the owner eats it once it gets a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: whenever it is known that the animal gave birth, the priest gets nothing here. Whenever it did not give birth, the offspring goes to the priest. If it is uncertain, it may be eaten by its owners once it has a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא replaces the age rule with a simple three-way rule. It depends only on what we actually know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no guessing based on age. A ספק בכור still has some holiness, so it cannot be used freely. It waits until it gets a מום, and then the owner (not the כהן) may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
A blemish that disqualifies an animal from the altar
The owners

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל decides by the animal's age. רבי עקיבא says only real knowledge counts, and in a ספק the owner keeps the animal and eats it once it has a מום.
steps.confusionAlert: In the ספק case the animal does not go to the כהן. It stays with the owner, who may eat it only after it gets a מום.

phrases.english: This is the rule: whenever it is known that it gave birth before,
the priest has nothing here;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה — הֲרֵי זֶה לַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: and whenever it did not give birth before, this goes to the priest;
and if it is uncertain, it is eaten in its blemished state by the owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the age rule, רבי עקיבא states his own principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If it is known the animal gave birth, the כהן gets nothing. If it is known it did not, the כהן gets the offspring. In a ספק, the owner eats it once it has a מום.

steps.title: Why is the older animal only a ספק? Most animals give birth in their first year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל. Past the first year we should rely on רוב: most animals get pregnant and give birth within their first year, so this one surely gave birth already.
steps.simpleTranslation: From then on, why is it uncertain? Follow the majority of animals. Most animals get pregnant and give birth within their first year, so this one surely gave birth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by questioning רבי ישמעאל's "from then on it is uncertain." It asks why we don't follow the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we follow רוב. Since most goats give birth in their first year, an older goat should be treated as having surely given birth already. Then its next male should be certainly not a בכור, not a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Follow the majority
Become pregnant and give birth

phrases.english: GEMARA: From here on, why is it uncertain?
phrases.notes: This quotes רבי ישמעאל's words in the משנה about an animal older than the age he gave.

phrases.english: Follow the majority of animals,
and most animals become pregnant and give birth
within their first year,
so this one certainly gave birth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing רבי ישמעאל's ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's ruling that an animal past the age limit is a ספק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of רוב says most animals give birth in their first year, so the older animal should count as having surely given birth.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר, who takes the מיעוט into account. That would explain why he treats the older animal as a ספק rather than relying on רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר, who is concerned about the minority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to its question. Maybe רבי ישמעאל belongs to the view of רבי מאיר, who doesn't fully rely on the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is known for worrying about the מיעוט. If רבי ישמעאל agrees with him, the few animals that don't give birth in their first year keep the case a ספק. The word לימא signals only a suggestion, and the גמרא will test it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion that may be rejected)
Is concerned for the minority
He holds

steps.confusionAlert: לימא is a tentative suggestion, not a final answer. The גמרא usually goes on to push it away.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Shall we say that Rabbi Yishmael holds like Rabbi Meir,
who is concerned for the minority?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a tentative answer to the קשיא from רוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the תנא to a known view (רבי מאיר) that does not rely fully on רוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל should follow the majority, like the usual rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps he is like רבי מאיר and considers the minority, so the case stays a ספק (this is still a suggestion).

steps.title: Even the רבנן only follow a majority that is in front of us
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רבי ישמעאל can follow the רבנן too, because the רבנן rely only on a visible majority, not a general pattern like most animals giving birth in their first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say רבי ישמעאל follows the רבנן. The רבנן follow the majority only when it is a majority in front of us, like nine stores or the סנהדרין. A majority that is not in front of us is different: there the רבנן do not follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question from Step 9, so we no longer have to say רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of רוב are now separated. One is a majority we can see right now, like counting stores or judges. The other is a general pattern, like 'most animals give birth in year one.' The רבנן rely only on the first kind, so the older animal stays a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say: introduces an answer that works even for the other opinion
A majority that is right in front of us, which we can actually count
A majority that is not in front of us: a general pattern of how things usually are
Nine stores: the classic case of a visible majority
The court of judges, which decides by majority vote

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן ignore רוב altogether. This answer says they ignore only a רוב that is not in front of us.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between a visible majority and a general-pattern majority comes up all over the גמרא.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis.
When they follow the majority,
it is with a majority that is in front of us,
such as nine stores and the Sanhedrin.
phrases.notes: Picture meat found near nine kosher shops and one non-kosher one, or judges voting: in both you can actually count the majority.

phrases.english: But with a majority that is not in front of us,
the Rabbis do not follow the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 9's question, in place of Step 10's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two kinds of רוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought only רבי מאיר could avoid relying on the רוב of animals giving birth in year one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the רבנן rely only on a רוב that is in front of us, so רבי ישמעאל fits their view too.

steps.title: Challenge: the רבנן follow a hidden majority with minors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that in the case of a קטן and קטנה, the majority is not in front of us, yet the רבנן still follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the case of a boy and girl who are minors. That is a majority that is not in front of us, and yet the רבנן do follow the majority, as we learned in a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in Step 11 and announces that a ברייתא will prove its point. This line sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 claimed that the רבנן never rely on a majority that is not in front of us. The גמרא says it has a case where they do. Whether a child will grow up normal is a general pattern, not something we can count.

keyTerms.meaning: But look: introduces a challenge from a known case
A boy and a girl who are minors
As we learned: introduces a quoted source

phrases.english: But there is the case of a boy and a girl who are minors,
which is a majority that is not in front of us,
and the Rabbis do follow the majority,
as we learned:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָטָן וּקְטַנָּה, דְּרוּבָּא דְּלֵיתֵיהּ קַמַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן do not follow a רוב that is not in front of us
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: the רבנן rely on the general pattern that most minors grow up able to have children.

steps.title: The ברייתא: minors do not do חליצה or יבום
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that minors do neither חליצה nor יבום. The רבנן agree about חליצה because the פסוק says 'man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy or girl who is a minor does not do חליצה and does not do יבום. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The רבנן said to him: you said well that they do not do חליצה. The word 'man' is written in that section, and we compare the woman to the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא it promised. The רבנן agree with רבי מאיר about חליצה but not yet about יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חליצה there is a clear source: the פסוק says 'איש,' an adult man. The woman is compared to him, so she must be an adult too. For יבום there is no such word, so the רבנן will ask רבי מאיר for his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that frees a widow from marrying her late husband's brother
Marriage of a childless widow to her late husband's brother
We compare: one case learns its law from another
The section of the תורה that deals with this topic

phrases.english: A boy or a girl who is a minor does not do chalitza
and does not do yibum.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
They said to him:
You said well that they do not do chalitza,
since "man" is written in the section,
and we compare the woman to the man.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָטָן וּקְטַנָּה לֹא חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַיבְּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source promised by 'דִּתְנַן' in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן follow a רוב that is not in front of us
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a קטן and קטנה and יבום

steps.title: The רבנן ask why minors cannot do יבום
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רבי מאיר for his reason about יבום, since the פסוק does not say 'man' there.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that minors do not do יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, the רבנן ask רבי מאיר to explain his ruling about יבום. This question sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'man' source from Step 13 covered only חליצה. Without a word in the פסוק, רבי מאיר needs a reason based on logic.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason that they do not do yibum?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the רבנן agreeing only about חליצה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי מאיר's reason for forbidding יבום to minors

steps.title: רבי מאיר worries about the minority who cannot have children
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that the boy might turn out to be a סריס or the girl an איילונית. Then there is no מצוה of יבום, and they would have married a forbidden relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: a boy might turn out to be a סריס, and a girl might turn out to be an איילונית. Then they would turn out to have been with a forbidden relative.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his reason: we cannot know yet whether the minor will grow up able to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום is allowed only to build a family for the brother who died. If the couple cannot have children, the brother's wife stays forbidden. רבי מאיר takes the small minority of such people into account, which matches his approach from Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who cannot father children
A woman who did not develop normally and cannot have children
A forbidden relationship
Run into, come upon

phrases.english: He said to them:
A boy: perhaps he will turn out to be a saris.
A girl: perhaps she will turn out to be an aylonis.
Then they would turn out to have come upon a forbidden relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: קָטָן — שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא סָרִיס
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Minors might turn out unable to have children. Then there is no מצוה, and the relationship is forbidden.

steps.title: The רבנן rely on most minors being normal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge. The רבנן follow the majority of minors, who are not סריסים or איילונית, even though that majority is not in front of us.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: go after the majority of boy minors, and most boys are not סריסים. Go after girl minors, and most girls are not איילונית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the רבנן's side and closes the challenge to Step 11. The רבנן clearly rely on a majority that is not in front of us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one can count the children who will grow up unable to have children. That is exactly the kind of general-pattern רוב Step 11 said the רבנן ignore. Yet here the רבנן rely on it, so the answer in Step 11 seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Go after: follow
They are

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about minors shows that the רבנן follow even a רוב that is not in front of us. So the answer in Step 11, that they follow only a visible majority, is challenged.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Go after the majority of boy minors,
and most boy minors are not sarisim.
Go after the girl minors,
and most girl minors are not aylonis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge's conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in Steps 13-15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11's claim that the רבנן ignore a רוב that is not in front of us
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן allow minors to do יבום because they rely on most children growing up normal, which is a majority not in front of us.

steps.title: רבא steps in with a new approach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets aside the earlier explanation because of the challenge in Step 16. It introduces רבא, who will give a fresh answer.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא drops the explanation that just failed and introduces רבא, whose new answer comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא tells us the earlier approach no longer stands. Step 16 showed that the רבנן do follow a majority that is not in front of us, so a new explanation is needed. רבא's actual words come right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous explanation is being dropped.
רבא said. This introduces a new view from the אמורא רבא.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for רבא's answer in this line. This line only introduces him, and his actual explanation comes next.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in Step 16 by dropping the earlier approach and opening a new one from רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement explanation: the earlier approach is abandoned and a new one is introduced. Its content comes in the next line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier view held that the רבנן do not follow a majority that is not in front of us.
steps.terutzMaskana: That view cannot stand because of the case of a קטן and קטנה, so רבא offers a different explanation.
